'''Harold H. Seward''' (July 24, 1930 – June 19, 2012) was a [[computer scientist]], [[engineer]], and [[inventor]]. Seward developed the [[radix sort]] and [[counting sort]] algorithms in 1954 at [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology|MIT]].<ref>{{Cite web |last1=Huang |first1=Chenn-Jung |last2=Guan |first2=Chih-Tai |last3=Chuang |first3=Yi-Ta |date= |title=Enhanced Generic Key-Address Mapping Sort Algorithm |url=http://par.cse.nsysu.edu.tw/~algo/paper/paper06/C15.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170705082052/http://par.cse.nsysu.edu.tw/~algo/paper/paper06/C15.pdf |archive-date=5 July 2017 |archive-format=PDF |access-date=2023-04-20 |page=2 }}</ref> He also worked on the [[Whirlwind Computer]] and developed instruments that powered the guidance systems for the [[Apollo spacecraft]] and [[Polaris missile]].<ref>{{ cite patent
 |country=US
 |number=3137794
 |status= patent
 |title=Directionally Sensitive Light Detector
 |gdate=1964-06-16
 |fdate=1960-06-28
 |invent1= Seward, Harold H.
}}</ref><ref>{{ cite patent

 |title=Two-Color Horizon Sensor
